subject: T34: MCM design direction commitment -- what I'm choosing not to do
body:
## T34: MCM Design Direction Commitment

FD taught: world-class designers make explicit commitments about what they WILL NOT do. This is a constraint, not a limitation.

### What MCM WILL NOT Do (GD's Commitment)

**1. No background color gradients.**
The Pistons palette is bold in hue, not in complexity. Gradients create visual noise that competes with math content. MCM uses flat backgrounds. If a gradient is ever proposed, GD will reject it.

**2. No purely decorative animation.**
Every animation in MCM must pass the question: 'what does the user understand better because this moved?' If there is no answer, the animation doesn't ship. (The correct-pulse passes: Kai knows he got it right before reading the text. The jersey stripe is static.)

**3. No color outside the Pistons palette for UI.**
The Pistons palette (#C8102E, #1D42BA, #002D62, #BEC0C2, neutral backgrounds) is sufficient. Chart colors and grade indicators use variants of these. Any new color requires Marcus sign-off.

**4. No toast-on-toast.**
MCM currently has 3 toast types (autosave, session restore, corruption banner). No fourth toast will be specced. If a new notification is needed, it replaces an existing pattern or becomes inline.

**5. No gamification that doesn't serve math mastery.**
Points, streaks, and badges are only valid if they correlate with math learning. The sparkline (score trend) is valid. An arbitrary 'streak counter' is not -- unless it tracks consecutive exams above 80%.

### Why This Matters

Each of these 'will nots' closes a design door permanently. That's uncomfortable. But Muriel Cooper's bar: every addition should improve coherence. These commitments improve coherence by reducing the decision space for future sprints.
